title: Inactivation of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza Viruses Using Deep Ultraviolet Radiation of at Different Wavelengths 波長の異なる深紫外線による高病原性鳥インフルエンザウイルスの不活化
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) of the H5N1 subtype have been reported to infect not only birds, but also humans, cattle, and other mammals, posing a serious public health concern and highlighting the need for effective control measures. Ultraviolet (UV) irradiation is widely known as an effective modality for virus inactivation, and recent advances in LED technology have enabled the generation of UV light of various wavelengths, each with distinct characteristics. In this study, we evaluated the efficacy of four different UV wavelengths (222 nm, 230 nm, 254 nm, and 265 nm) in inactivating HPAIVs. HPAIV at a concentration of 2.0 × 106 plaque-forming units (PFU) /mL was irradiated with UV light at doses ranging from 0 to 7.3 mJ/cm2. The UV doses required to achieve a 99.9% reduction in the viral titer were 4.2 mJ, 4.9 mJ, 5.6 mJ, and 4.3 mJ for UV light wavelengths of 222 nm, 230 nm, 254 nm, and 265 nm, respectively. All four UV light wavelengths reduced viral titers by more than 99.9%, demonstrating their effectiveness in inactivating HPAIVs. This study demonstrated that UV light at all the four tested wavelengths effectively inactivated HPAIVs to a comparable extent, suggesting the usefulness of UV light for inactivating HPAIVs in a wide range of environments.

title: Peru’s only penguin species at risk from upcoming El Niño and bird flu, experts warn
abstract: SAN JUAN DE MARCONA, Peru — First, there was the H5N1 avian influenza of 2022, then El Niño arrived in 2023, disrupting coastal waters and fish availability. For Peru’s Humboldt penguins, the only species of penguins that breeds in the country, the burden was too heavy: Its population dropped by two-thirds between 2022 and 2025.

analysis.methods: The study analyzes population trends and environmental disruptions, specifically examining the effects of H5N1 avian influenza and El Niño on the penguins' habitat and food availability.
analysis.main_results: Peru's Humboldt penguin population decreased by two-thirds between 2022 and 2025, attributed to the combined impacts of H5N1 avian influenza and El Niño.

analysis.summary_en: Peru's Humboldt penguin population has declined by two-thirds between 2022 and 2025, primarily due to the combined effects of H5N1 avian influenza and El Niño. The avian influenza outbreak in 2022 and subsequent El Niño event disrupted coastal waters and fish availability, creating an unsustainable burden on the only penguin species breeding in Peru. Experts warn that these dual threats highlight the species' extreme vulnerability, necessitating urgent conservation measures and enhanced surveillance for both avian influenza and climate-related impacts on marine ecosystems.

But since 2022, the species’ has been under pressure from the spread of avian influenza, followed by El Niño.Between 2022 and 2025, the population of Humboldt penguins has dropped by two-thirds across 34 islands and peninsulas on the Peruvian coast.Experts monitoring the species say penguins are abandoning their nests as they already feel the impacts of the upcoming El Niño episode, which changes temperatures in coastal waters and diminishes the amount of prey fish available.Scientists are asking both the national government and the IUCN to revise the species’ status to reflect the increasing threats and boost conservation efforts.See All Key Ideas SAN JUAN DE MARCONA, Peru — First, there was the H5N1 avian influenza of 2022, then El Niño arrived in 2023, disrupting coastal waters and fish availability. For Peru’s Humboldt penguins, the only species of penguins that breeds in the country, the burden was too heavy: Its population dropped by two-thirds between 2022 and 2025. Still recovering, the species is now facing a super El Niño that could further undermine its future. In early June, the Secretary-General of the United Nations, António Guterres, warned: “The science is clear: El Niño is arriving on our doorstep in the coming months with 90% certainty. The world must treat it as the urgent climate warning it is. El Niño conditions will pour fuel on the fire of a warming world. Impacts will hit even harder, travel even farther, and cross borders with devastating speed.” Scientists studying the Humboldt penguins (Spheniscus humboldti) in Peru say that they are already feeling the impact of the 2026 El Niño as warmer coastal waters drive the cold current carrying the main prey fish, Peruvian anchovy (Engraulis ringens) or anchoveta, deeper and further offshore. That means the penguins and other seabirds are forced to undertake longer fishing trips to get enough food to breed or feed chicks. Scientists studying El Niño say the gaps between the events are getting smaller and the effects are more unpredictable. “Climate change is driving more frequent and more severe El Niño events,” Andres Lescano, director of Clima, the Latin American Center of Excellence in Climate Change and Health, told Mongabay. The Humboldt penguin nests and rests in the coastal deserts of southern Peru and northern Chile’s arid Pacific coastline and offshore islands, which are directly affected by El Niño events. In Punta San Juan de Marcona National Reserve, one of the penguins’ major nesting colonies in southern Peru, the number of penguin nests has halved between April and May 2026, from 190 on April 10 to 94 on May 30, according to scientists’ recordings. “They abandoned their nests,” Peruvian biologist Susana Cardénas, the director of the Punta San Juan program, told Mongabay at the 54-hectare (133 acres) marine reserve, where she leads a team that monitors the Humboldt penguin population. El Niño undermines food availability for the Humboldt penguin, leading to breeding failure and nest abandonment. Image courtesy of Punta San Juan program. Image by Ann Knutson. “There was a reduction in food availability and when the parent that stays with the egg gets too hungry, it leaves,” she said. “The [Humboldt] penguin is the sentinel species, and its breeding failure is a sign that it’s going to get worse. It’s going to be a really bad year for all the seabirds.” The Humboldt penguin breeds from April to August and from September until December, before other seabirds, so it is the first to be impacted by the shortage of food caused by the warmer sea surface temperatures, which have risen by up to 2° Celsius (3.6° Fahrenheit) in the eastern equatorial Pacific, according to Peru’s official National Study of the El Niño Phenomenon. Punta San Juan de Marcona serves as a marine biodiversity hotspot with large breeding populations of seabirds, including the Humboldt penguin, the Peruvian pelican (Pelecanus thagus), the Guanay cormorant (Leucocarbo bougainvillii), the Peruvian booby (Sula variegata), and hundreds-strong breeding colonies of Peruvian fur seal (Arctocephalus australis ssp) and South American sea lions (Otaria byronia), as well as a small population of marine otters (Lontra felina). The Humboldt current, which flows up from Antarctica, allows the upwelling of nutrients, which supports a huge biomass of anchoveta as well as a variety of seabirds, sea lions and fur seals. Peru’s coast is one of the third or fourth richest fisheries in the world. However, as sea surface temperatures began to rise, Peru’s Production and Fisheries Ministry announced on June 11 that it was closing the anchoveta fishing season in the country’s north-central coast as a “conservation measure” based on scientific information from the Peruvian Sea Institute (IMARPE). The burden of disease After the H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) hit South America in late 2022, the virus caused a massive drop in seabird and marine mammal numbers in 2022 and 2023, on its Pacific and Atlantic coasts. In Peru alone, the virus killed about 558,000 seabirds across 14 species (including cormorants, boobies, pelicans, seagulls, terns and penguins) and 11,000 sea lions between December 2022 and December 2023, according to a 2025 study published by the Society for Conservation Biology. Peru’s seabird population was particularly hard hit, accounting for the vast majority of bird deaths, with an estimated 667,000 total on South America’s Pacific and Atlantic coasts. But bird species continued to be battered by the ensuing El Niño. As sea temperatures peaked at nearly 4 °C (7.2° F) higher than normal in the last year, penguins and other seabirds were forced to undertake longer fishing trips, often exposing the chicks or fledglings to predators, starvation, nest abandonment by the parent birds, or, in some cases, the shortage of food can mean that the penguins do not breed at all. In Punta San Juan, not a single penguin nest was recorded in 2023. “This is unprecedented since records began,” explained Cárdenas, who runs the Punta San Juan program through the Centre for Environmental Sustainability at Lima’s Cayetano Heredia University. “The penguins were getting ready for their breeding season; the marine conditions changed and they did not come back to breed.” The Humboldt penguin is the only penguin species breeding in Peru. Image courtesy of the Punta San Juan program. Image by Michael Tweddle. A census of the penguins in 34 islands and peninsulas along the Peruvian coast showed that their numbers dropped from 15,663 in 2022 to approximately 5,400 in 2025, according to a census carried out by Cayetano Heredia University and the NGO Peruvian Association for the Conservation of Nature (APECO) and other organizations, along with Peru’s Forestry and Wildlife Service, SERFOR. Since 2023, constant monitoring of the population by scientists at the Punta San Juan reserve has detected a slow recovery in numbers, until the early effects of the 2026 El Niño caused a new wave of nest abandonment. In July, local Peruvian media was reporting the deaths of marine birds, including penguins, as well as marine mammals such as South American sea lions along the coast due to a lack of food. As the Humboldt Penguin faces an onslaught of threats, Cárdenas and other scientists in Peru are asking the government to change its conservation status from endangered to critically endangered. The move had been approved by a supreme decree in 2021, but it still needs presidential approval to be signed into law. Scientists from Peru and Chile are also pushing the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species to update the classification of the penguin from vulnerable to endangered amid the decline in its numbers. In January 2025, SERFOR announced a National Conservation Plan for the Humboldt penguin and the sea otter, but, despite a series of workshops with conservationists and environmental nonprofits, the plan has yet to be published. title: Genetic determinants of cell- and egg-preferred replication in H3N2 canine influenza virus.
abstract: The H3N2 canine influenza virus (CIV), which originated from avian influenza viruses and has circulated in dogs for over two decades, remains poorly understood in terms of its host adaptation mechanisms and cellular tropism. In this study, we isolated two phenotypically distinct H3N2 CIV strains (CX3 and CX12) from a canine respiratory disease outbreak. Although both were isolated using MDCK cells, CX3 showed higher replication efficiency and plaque-forming ability in MDCK cells, whereas CX12 replicated more efficiently in chicken embryos. Using reverse genetics, we identified the PB1 gene as a critical enhancer of viral polymerase activity and the HA gene as a key contributor to viral stability, both of which collectively mediate cell-preferred replication. These findings provide mechanistic insights into H3N2 CIV host adaptation and offer a foundation for future vaccine development.

title: Evolution of swine influenza surveillance and one health governance in Taiwan: from zoonotic risk management to integrated preparedness.
abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) remain a persistent global threat because of rapid antigenic change, frequent genetic reassortment, and cross-species transmission. Swine act as key "mixing vessels," permitting co-infection with avian and human strains and accelerating viral diversification and zoonotic risk. Effective veterinary surveillance is therefore critical for detecting viral evolution within swine populations and for providing early warning at the animal-human interface. Taiwan, home to approximately 5.5 million pigs and 23.4 million people, offers a representative case for examining how swine influenza surveillance has evolved in response to these challenges. This review describes the development of veterinary surveillance strategies from fragmented, event-driven monitoring to a coordinated One Health governance framework incorporating routine whole-genome sequencing, targeted serological surveillance, and coordinated data exchange across sectors. Key historical milestones include mass vaccination and culling programs, the 2009 pandemic response and recent zoonotic detections of H1N2v in humans (2021-2023), collectively evidencing ongoing bidirectional viral exchange. Episodes of severe human seasonal influenza activity, including H3N2-associated outbreaks, further highlighted the importance of coordinated surveillance across human and animal health sectors. By focusing on surveillance practices applied to animals, this review highlights the practical value of integrating molecular epidemiology, veterinary field monitoring, artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled technologies and cross-sector communication under a One Health framework. The Taiwanese experience demonstrates how strengthened veterinary surveillance can improve the sensitivity for detecting reassortment events, enhance traceability of viral spread, and support timely risk assessment in intensive livestock systems. These lessons offer a practical, replicable pathway for other countries aiming to overcome swine influenza surveillance fragmentation and strengthen pandemic preparedness under a One Health framework.

title: A lethal human H5N5 influenza virus isolate exhibits low pandemic risk traits
abstract: In fall of 2025, a fatal infection of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) virus H5N5 occurred. To define the risk of this emerging virus to humans, we performed a comprehensive analysis based on our established triage. Serological analysis revealed that humans across all birth years had no detectable neutralizing antibodies to this H5N5 isolate. Further characterization revealed a lack of phenotypic signatures associated with epidemiologically successful influenza viruses in humans, including reduced replication in human airway cells and an avian-like pH of inactivation. Additionally, assessment of H5N5 in ferrets revealed a lack of direct contact transmission and moderate disease severity. H5N5 infection in ferrets with prior immunity against the 2009 H1N1 pandemic strain resulted in fewer clinical signs and reduced viral shedding. Together our data suggest that the current H5N5 HPAI lineage poses a low pandemic risk.

title: Evolution is Not Always Bifurcating: ATLAZ and the Geometric Resolution of Reticulate Virology
abstract: Abstract The reliance on strictly bifurcating phylogenetic trees fundamentally distorts the evolutionary history of reticulate viral populations. Traditional maximum-likelihood algorithms mandate vertical descent, imposing artificial clades upon recombinant genomes and obscuring the origins of segmented pandemic shifts. Furthermore, linear selection metrics (e.g., dN/dS) fail mathematically when evaluating overlapping open reading frames. Here, ATLAZ (Alignment, Topology, and Lineage Analysis in Zig) is presented as a memory-deterministic geometric engine that explicitly bypasses the phylogenetic tree to track the major transition from tree-like to reticulate evolution. By computing Vietoris-Rips simplicial complexes and extracting H1 persistence directly from spatial distance matrices, ATLAZ definitively isolates horizontal recombination in Hepatitis B and Avian Influenza. Conversely, the absence of topological loops strictly proves the clonal descent of Ebola, Zika, and Marburg viruses. Utilizing a native Galois Field reduction across a zero-copy C-ABI boundary, ATLAZ processes massive cohorts (over 6,000 sequences) with memory strictly bounded by the sparse filtration cutoff, shattering the catastrophic computational bottlenecks of previous Topological Data Analysis frameworks. Furthermore, sequential column ablation calculates a novel Topological Selection Score (TSS), geometrically mapping absolute structural rigidity and identifying optimal targets for direct-acting antivirals in seconds. ATLAZ establishes a new absolute, math-driven standard for tracking major transitions in computational virology.

abstract_zh: 摘要 对严格分叉的系统发育树的依赖从根本上扭曲了网状病毒种群的进化历史。传统的最大似然算法要求垂直下降,将人工进化枝强加于重组 基因组 上,并模糊了分段流行病转变的起源。此外,在评估重叠的开放阅读框时,线性选择指标(例如 dN/dS)在数学上会失败。在这里,ATLAZ(Zig 中的对齐、拓扑和谱系分析)被视为一种内存确定性几何引擎,它明确绕过系统发育树来跟踪从树状到网状 进化 的主要转变。通过计算 Vietoris-Rips 单纯复合体并直接从空间距离矩阵中提取 H1 持久性,ATLAZ 明确分离了乙型肝炎和 禽流感 中的水平重组。相反,拓扑环的缺失严格证明了埃博拉病毒、寨卡病毒和马尔堡病毒的克隆血统。利用跨零拷贝 C-ABI 边界的原生伽罗瓦域缩减,ATLAZ 可以处理大量 队列研究(超过 6,000 个序列),内存严格受稀疏过滤截断限制,打破了先前拓扑数据分析框架的灾难性计算瓶颈。此外,顺序列消融计算出一种新颖的拓扑选择分数(TSS),以几何方式映射绝对结构刚性并在几秒钟内确定直接作用的 抗病毒药物 的最佳目标。ATLAZ 建立了一个新的绝对的、数学驱动的标准,用于跟踪计算病毒学的重大转变。

title: Elicitation of stem-directed antibodies in rhesus macaques by a conventional hemagglutinin immunogen
abstract: Because they can bind many strains of influenza, antibodies targeting the hemagglutinin (HA) stem have been attractive targets for vaccine development. Many monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) directed at the HA stem have been isolated from humans, and these mAbs have mediated broad protection in animal models. We describe here HA stem-directed mAbs isolated from rhesus macaques immunized with an "ordinary" H1 HA trimer. All immunized rhesus macaques developed high serum titers with broad reactivity to diverse H1N1 and H5N1 viruses, and 7 isolated mAbs strongly blocked canonical stem antibody CR6261 binding to H1. MAb DH726.1 robustly protected mice from lethal challenge with H1N1 and H5N1 viruses, and cryo-EM showed the binding footprint overlapped that of some human mAbs. These findings suggest that vaccination with the standard, trimeric HA immunogens may be sufficient to elicit stem antibodies at titers adequate to protect against zoonotic H5N1 influenza.

title_zh: 通过常规血凝素免疫原在恒河猴中诱导干定向抗体
source_body_en: Because they can bind many strains of influenza, antibodies targeting the hemagglutinin (HA) stem have been attractive targets for vaccine development. Many monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) directed at the HA stem have been isolated from humans, and these mAbs have mediated broad protection in animal models. We describe here HA stem-directed mAbs isolated from rhesus macaques immunized with an "ordinary" H1 HA trimer. All immunized rhesus macaques developed high serum titers with broad reactivity to diverse H1N1 and H5N1 viruses, and 7 isolated mAbs strongly blocked canonical stem antibody CR6261 binding to H1. MAb DH726.1 robustly protected mice from lethal challenge with H1N1 and H5N1 viruses, and cryo-EM showed the binding footprint overlapped that of some human mAbs. These findings suggest that vaccination with the standard, trimeric HA immunogens may be sufficient to elicit stem antibodies at titers adequate to protect against zoonotic H5N1 influenza.

title: Integrated in silico and in vitro approaches reveal novel coumarin hybrids targeting influenza A virus RNA-dependent RNA polymerase.
abstract: ABSTRACT: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a significant public health threat due to its high mutation rate and increasing resistance to existing antiviral drugs. The viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) is essential for viral replication and represents a promising target for new therapeutics. We screened our in-house chemical library of 103 compounds against two domains of the IAV RdRp complex using molecular docking. Based on computational findings, we selected eleven coumarin-phenolic acid hybrids and one thiazolidinone compounds for in vitro evaluation against H1N1 and H5N1. LMed 93 and LMed 99 exhibited potent antiviral activity, with EC 50 values of 5.66 and 1.21 μM against H1N1 respectively, and high selectivity indices. Mechanistic studies showed that LMed 99 acts throughout early to late stages of infection, while LMed 93 impacts early and intermediate stages. Both compounds significantly inhibited viral RNA synthesis, with LMed 99 achieving 82% inhibition at 1- and 3-hours post-infection (hpi) and 80% at 6 hpi, and LMed 93 achieving 82% (1 hpi), 78% (3 hpi), and 60% (6 hpi). LMed 99 reduced viral proteins and mRNA in a time-dependent manner, indicating interference with viral transcription. A mini-replicon assay showed that LMed 93, at 70 and 35 μM, reduces polymerase activity by 53.7% and 38.7%, while LMed 99 at 9 and 4.5 μM increased expression by 108.97% and 61.37%, respectively. Structure–activity relationship analysis highlighted that catechol groups and halogenation enhance antiviral potency. These findings suggest that LMed 93 and LMed 99 are promising coumarin-based scaffolds for developing new anti-Influenza A agents, also offering potential strategies for combating other RNA viruses.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 由于 突变 的高发病率以及对现有 抗病毒药物 药物的耐药性不断增加,甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 仍然是一个重大的公共卫生威胁。该研究旨在鉴定针对 IAV RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶 (RdRp) 的新型化合物来应对这一挑战。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用计算机和体外方法来筛选针对 IAV RdRp 复合物的化合物。它重点关注 禽流感 A 病毒,特别是 H5N1,并评估了所选化合物的 抗病毒药物 体外活性。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员利用分子对接筛选了针对 IAV RdRp 复合物两个结构域的 103 种化合物。根据计算结果,他们选择了 11 种香豆素-酚酸杂化物和一种噻唑烷酮化合物,用于针对 H1N1 和 H5N1 的体外评估。
elements_zh.main_results: LMed 93 和 LMed 99 表现出有效的 抗病毒药物 活性,针对 H1N1 的 EC 50 值分别为 5.66 和 1.21 μM,并且具有高选择性指数。两种化合物均显着抑制病毒 RNA 合成,LMed 99 在感染后 1 小时和 3 小时 (hpi) 时实现了 82% 的抑制,在 6 hpi 时实现了 80% 的抑制,LMed 93 实现了 82% (1 hpi)、78% (3 hpi) 和 60% (6 hpi)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,LMed 93 和 LMed 99 是有前途的基于香豆素的支架,可用于开发新型抗甲型流感药物,为对抗其他 RNA 病毒提供潜在策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果为针对 IAV RdRp 的新 抗病毒药物 药物的开发提供了见解,这可以增强 禽流感 暴发 的 监测 和 治疗 选项。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于体外研究结果和计算筛选,可能无法完全反映体内疗效。证据是中等的,因为它不包括临床试验或长期影响。

title_zh: 综合计算机和体外方法揭示了针对甲型流感病毒 RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶的新型香豆素杂合体。
source_body_en: ABSTRACT: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a significant public health threat due to its high mutation rate and increasing resistance to existing antiviral drugs. The viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) is essential for viral replication and represents a promising target for new therapeutics. We screened our in-house chemical library of 103 compounds against two domains of the IAV RdRp complex using molecular docking. Based on computational findings, we selected eleven coumarin-phenolic acid hybrids and one thiazolidinone compounds for in vitro evaluation against H1N1 and H5N1. LMed 93 and LMed 99 exhibited potent antiviral activity, with EC 50 values of 5.66 and 1.21 μM against H1N1 respectively, and high selectivity indices. Mechanistic studies showed that LMed 99 acts throughout early to late stages of infection, while LMed 93 impacts early and intermediate stages. Both compounds significantly inhibited viral RNA synthesis, with LMed 99 achieving 82% inhibition at 1- and 3-hours post-infection (hpi) and 80% at 6 hpi, and LMed 93 achieving 82% (1 hpi), 78% (3 hpi), and 60% (6 hpi). LMed 99 reduced viral proteins and mRNA in a time-dependent manner, indicating interference with viral transcription. A mini-replicon assay showed that LMed 93, at 70 and 35 μM, reduces polymerase activity by 53.7% and 38.7%, while LMed 99 at 9 and 4.5 μM increased expression by 108.97% and 61.37%, respectively. Structure–activity relationship analysis highlighted that catechol groups and halogenation enhance antiviral potency. These findings suggest that LMed 93 and LMed 99 are promising coumarin-based scaffolds for developing new anti-Influenza A agents, also offering potential strategies for combating other RNA viruses.

title: The One Health Blind Spot at the Human‒Animal Interface in US Influenza Surveillance.
abstract: Novel influenza A viruses have cost thousands of lives and billions of dollars of economic losses in the 21st century, and 2 of the past 4 pandemic influenza A viruses likely originated in animal populations on the North American continent. Despite this, the human and veterinary influenza surveillance systems in the United States are poorly connected and have fallen short of congressional mandates for data sharing and interoperability. This places the United States in a reactive posture that is focused on containment of outbreaks that have already occurred rather than proactive surveillance and prevention. The significant investments in surveillance infrastructure and genomic technologies spurred by the COVID-19 pandemic, along with the new National One Health Framework, present a unique opportunity to modernize influenza surveillance with a greater emphasis on the interconnectedness of human and animal health. However, funding for enhanced surveillance is set to decrease significantly as pandemic-era funding sunsets. Continuing investments into novel surveillance technologies have been critical in addressing the recent H5N1 influenza outbreaks and will be critical to prevent future economic losses and losses of both human and animal life. ( Am J Public Health . 2026;116(8):1220-1228. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308445).

analysis.summary_en: This paper highlights a critical blind spot in US influenza surveillance, where human and veterinary systems remain poorly connected despite congressional mandates for data sharing. The reactive posture of the US, focused on containment rather than prevention, contrasts with opportunities presented by COVID-19-era investments in genomic technologies and the National One Health Framework. However, funding for enhanced surveillance is set to decrease, threatening progress. The authors emphasize that continued investments in novel surveillance technologies are essential for addressing recent H5N1 outbreaks and preventing future economic and human losses, advocating for a more integrated One Health approach to influenza surveillance.

title: Analysis of Influenza A viruses using the resonant recognition model
abstract: Bird flu (Avian influenza) and human flu are both caused by Influenza A viruses, but they differ significantly in their host adaptation, transmission and severity. Here, we have used the Resonant Recognition Model (RRM), which is innovative approach using knowledge from quantum physics, biochemistry and mathematics, capable to analyse interactions between proteins and their targets, including other proteins, DNA, RNA, or small molecules. Using the RRM model we have identified different characteristics for different types of flu viruses, and we have found that there are three groups of flu viruses with completely different interactions with host cells receptors. Such finding can provide explanation why different flu viruses can interact only with specific hosts and why there is extremely low cross infection between different species, in particular between birds and humans.
journal: International Journal of Science and Research Archive

title: Enhancing knowledge on influenza and other pandemic threats for healthcare personnel readiness in Thailand, 2007–2024
abstract: Healthcare personnel are often the first line of defense against emerging diseases. Enhancing knowledge on influenza for healthcare personnel is part of Thailand’s influenza pandemic preparedness plan. Beginning in 2007, the Thailand Department of Medical Services organized trainings for Thai healthcare personnel in Bangkok and all regions of Thailand on prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and control of human seasonal, avian, and pandemic influenza. The curriculum included overviews on the global situation, clinical features and treatment, influenza epidemiology and burden in Thailand, influenza as a cause of pneumonia, laboratory diagnostics, impact of influenza in high-risk populations and increased risk for complications; influenza economic evaluation of seasonal influenza vaccination in Thailand, and immunization and planning for human influenza outbreaks. Topics initially focused on seasonal and pandemic influenza and expanded in scope to incorporate other pandemic threats, such as MERS-CoV and COVID-19. From August 2007 through December 2024, 114 trainings were conducted. A total of 26,422 attendees (range 10–700 per training) were trained, including clinicians, nurses, pharmacists, laboratory technicians, and public health scientists (professionals trained in epidemiology, disease surveillance, and health data analysis) from public and private hospitals from national, regional, provincial, and district levels in Bangkok and 41 provinces nationwide. During training sessions, participants reported that the program increased their readiness and self-reported confidence to respond to potential respiratory outbreaks. These capacity-building efforts contributed to a health workforce that was better positioned to respond to emerging respiratory threats, including the first wave of COVID-19. Educating healthcare personnel about prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and control of influenza is an important component of pandemic preparedness. Refresher courses or online tutorials may be needed periodically to maintain current knowledge.

title: Aerosol transmission of infectious diseases in poultry: microbiology, pathogenesis, and control measures
abstract: The expansion of intensive poultry production improves productivity but increases the risk of disease transmission. In poultry houses, infectious disease transmission occurs through direct and indirect routes, including surface contamination and vector-borne transmission. Typically, disease control in poultry mostly focuses on direct contact and management-related practices in poultry houses, but there is growing evidence highlighting the significance of the aerosol transmission route – an indirect route of pathogen spread that can impair production performance in poultry. High stocking density in poultry houses, inadequate ventilation, and poor biosecurity measures increase the risk of aerosolized transmission of bacterial, viral, and fungal pathogens. The efficiency of this route depends on particle size, humidity, temperature, and ventilation, which influence pathogen survival and exposure, and is further compounded by environmental stressors and the site of action within the animal’s respiratory system. Given that major pathogens, such as avian influenza virus, infectious bronchitis virus, avian orthoavulavirus 1, and Aspergillus spp., are usually transmitted via the aerosol route, it is essential for poultry farmers to adopt a range of mitigation strategies to achieve effective disease prevention and improve production output. As such, this review highlights the role of aerosol transmission in poultry health and management, focusing on microbiological aspects, pathogenesis, overall impact, and mitigation strategies. Also, this review aims to integrate current knowledge on aerosol characteristics with transmission dynamics and to provide insight into future research opportunities.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 集约化家禽生产的扩大提高了生产力,但增加了疾病 传播 的风险,突出表明需要了解气溶胶 传播 作为病原体传播的间接途径。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本综述重点关注微生物方面、发病机制 以及与禽舍中气溶胶 传播 相关的缓解策略,其中饲养密度高、通风不足和生物安全性差会增加 传播 风险。
elements_zh.methods: 该综述将当前关于气溶胶特征的知识与 传播 动力学相结合,检查了影响病原体存活和暴露的颗粒大小、湿度、温度和通风等因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 主要病原体有禽流感病毒、传染性支气管炎病毒、禽正鸟病毒1型、曲霉属等。通过气溶胶途径传播,其效率取决于环境条件和压力源。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者强调,气雾剂 传播 是家禽疾病控制中的一种重要但未被充分重视的途径,需要有针对性的缓解策略来提高生产性能。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 采用针对气溶胶的缓解策略对于家禽养殖户预防疾病和提高产量至关重要,特别是针对主要病原体。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 作为回顾,该研究综合了现有知识,但可能缺乏原始数据;然而,由于气溶胶动力学和病原体特异性 传播 数据的综合整合,证据强度中等。

title_zh: 家禽传染病气溶胶传播:微生物学、发病机制和控制措施
source_body_en: The expansion of intensive poultry production improves productivity but increases the risk of disease transmission. In poultry houses, infectious disease transmission occurs through direct and indirect routes, including surface contamination and vector-borne transmission. Typically, disease control in poultry mostly focuses on direct contact and management-related practices in poultry houses, but there is growing evidence highlighting the significance of the aerosol transmission route – an indirect route of pathogen spread that can impair production performance in poultry. High stocking density in poultry houses, inadequate ventilation, and poor biosecurity measures increase the risk of aerosolized transmission of bacterial, viral, and fungal pathogens. The efficiency of this route depends on particle size, humidity, temperature, and ventilation, which influence pathogen survival and exposure, and is further compounded by environmental stressors and the site of action within the animal’s respiratory system. Given that major pathogens, such as avian influenza virus, infectious bronchitis virus, avian orthoavulavirus 1, and Aspergillus spp., are usually transmitted via the aerosol route, it is essential for poultry farmers to adopt a range of mitigation strategies to achieve effective disease prevention and improve production output. As such, this review highlights the role of aerosol transmission in poultry health and management, focusing on microbiological aspects, pathogenesis, overall impact, and mitigation strategies. Also, this review aims to integrate current knowledge on aerosol characteristics with transmission dynamics and to provide insight into future research opportunities.

title: Twenty-Two Months of Syndromic Multiplex-PCR Testing for Acute Infections in a Southern Italian Hospital: Pathogen Epidemiology, Diagnostic Appropriateness and the Cost of Negative Results
abstract: Syndromic multiplex-PCR panels deliver rapid, comprehensive detection of pathogens and resistance determinants in acute infections, but their unrestricted use can generate a high proportion of negative results with substantial economic and stewardship implications. We retrospectively analysed all BioFire FilmArray meningitis/encephalitis (ME), upper-respiratory (RP2.1), pneumonia (PN) and gastrointestinal (GI) determinations performed at the UOSD Microbiology and Virology of P.O. “Vito Fazzi”, ASL Lecce (Apulia, Italy) between 1 July 2024 and 30 April 2026. Repeat determinations from the same patient with the same panel were identified in the laboratory information system and removed before any analysis, so that each determination analysed corresponds to a distinct diagnostic episode. Across 5381 determinations (CNS, n = 761; upper respiratory, n = 2601; lower respiratory, n = 399; gastrointestinal, n = 1620), 59.3% were negative for every target, with a steep appropriateness gradient: 90.0% negativity for the ME panel and 77.1% for the gastrointestinal panel versus 44.2% for the upper-respiratory and 26.6% for the pneumonia panel. CNS positives were predominantly viral (75%), led by enterovirus; Streptococcus pneumoniae was the only consistent bacterial agent. Human rhinovirus/enterovirus dominated the respiratory ecology; influenza A was almost entirely H3 and H1N1pdm09, but 8.1% of influenza-A–positive specimens were equivocal or non-subtypeable and were never referred for sequencing, an avoidable surveillance blind spot for novel/zoonotic (avian) influenza. Pneumonia-panel resistance markers (mecA/C–MREJ, CTX-M, KPC, NDM) clustered in Enterobacterales co-infections. The gastrointestinal panel was dominated by diarrhoeagenic Escherichia coli pathotypes (chiefly EPEC and EAEC) and Clostridioides difficile toxin, its 77% negativity identifying a second over-utilised stream. We argue for CSF-pleocytosis gating, tiered/reflex respiratory algorithms, gastrointestinal-panel gating to community-onset diarrhoea, and mandatory reflex sequencing of unsubtypeable influenza A.

title_original: Twenty-Two Months of Syndromic Multiplex-PCR Testing for Acute Infections in a Southern Italian Hospital: Pathogen Epidemiology, Diagnostic Appropriateness and the Cost of Negative Results

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the epidemiology, diagnostic appropriateness, and cost implications of syndromic multiplex-PCR testing for acute infections in a Southern Italian hospital, focusing on the high proportion of negative results and their economic impact.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective analysis of all BioFire FilmArray meningitis/encephalitis (ME), upper-respiratory (RP2.1), pneumonia (PN), and gastrointestinal (GI) determinations performed at the UOSD Microbiology and Virology of P.O. 'Vito Fazzi', ASL Lecce (Apulia, Italy) between 1 July 2024 and 30 April 2026, with repeat determinations removed to ensure distinct diagnostic episodes.
analysis.methods: The study involved analysing 5381 determinations across four syndromic panels (CNS, upper respiratory, lower respiratory, gastrointestinal) to assess pathogen detection rates, diagnostic appropriateness, and resistance markers, with a focus on identifying avoidable surveillance blind spots like unsubtypeable influenza A.
analysis.main_results: Across 5381 determinations, 59.3% were negative for every target, with negativity rates varying by panel: 90.0% for ME, 77.1% for GI, 44.2% for upper-respiratory, and 26.6% for pneumonia. CNS positives were predominantly viral (75%), led by enterovirus, and Streptococcus pneumoniae was the only consistent bacterial agent. Influenza A was almost entirely H3 and H1N1pdm09, but 8.1% were equivocal or non-subtypeable and not referred for sequencing.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the high negativity rates as evidence of over-utilization of certain panels, particularly ME and GI, and highlighted the avoidable surveillance gap for unsubtypeable influenza A, which could miss novel or zoonotic strains. The novelty lies in the detailed epidemiological mapping of pathogen distribution and resistance patterns across multiple syndromic panels.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for targeted diagnostic strategies, such as CSF-pleocytosis gating for CNS testing, tiered respiratory algorithms, and mandatory reflex sequencing of unsubtypeable influenza A, to improve diagnostic appropriateness and surveillance for potential zoonotic influenza threats.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and single-center setting, which may affect generalizability. However, the large sample size and comprehensive analysis provide moderate evidence strength for informing local diagnostic practices and surveillance protocols.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study evaluated syndromic multiplex-PCR testing over 22 months in a Southern Italian hospital, analysing 5381 determinations across CNS, respiratory, and gastrointestinal panels. A high proportion (59.3%) of results were negative, with rates varying by panel (90.0% for meningitis/encephalitis, 77.1% for gastrointestinal, 44.2% for upper-respiratory, and 26.6% for pneumonia). CNS positives were predominantly viral (75%), led by enterovirus, while Streptococcus pneumoniae was the only consistent bacterial agent. Influenza A was mostly H3 and H1N1pdm09, but 8.1% were unsubtypeable and not sequenced, representing a surveillance gap. The authors recommend targeted strategies like CSF-pleocytosis gating and mandatory sequencing of unsubtypeable influenza A to improve diagnostic appropriateness and zoonotic surveillance.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估意大利南部一家医院急性感染综合征多重 PCR 检测的 流行病学、诊断适当性和成本影响,重点关注阴性结果的高比例及其经济影响。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对在 UOSD 微生物学和病毒学中心进行的所有 BioFire FilmArray 脑膜炎/脑炎 (ME)、上呼吸道 (RP2.1)、肺炎 (PN) 和胃肠道 (GI) 测定的回顾性分析。“Vito Fazzi”,ASL 莱切(意大利普利亚)于 2024 年 7 月 1 日至 2026 年 4 月 30 日期间进行,删除了重复测定以确保不同的诊断事件。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究涉及分析四个综合征组(中枢神经系统、上呼吸道、下呼吸道、胃肠道)的 5381 项测定结果,以评估病原体检出率、诊断适当性和耐药标记物,重点是识别可避免的 监测 盲点,例如无法分型的甲型流感。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 5381 项测定中,每个目标的阴性率为 59.3%,阴性率因小组而异:ME 为 90.0%,GI 为 77.1%,上呼吸道为 44.2%,肺炎为 26.6%。中枢神经系统阳性主要是病毒(75%),以肠道病毒为首,肺炎链球菌是唯一一致的细菌病原体。甲型流感几乎全部是 H3 和 H1N1pdm09,但 8.1% 是模棱两可或不可分型的,并且未转介进行测序。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将高阴性率解释为过度使用某些组合的证据,特别是 ME 和 GI,并强调了不可亚型甲型流感的可避免的 监测 差距,这可能会错过新的或人畜共患的毒株。新颖之处在于跨多个综合征组的病原体分布和耐药模式的详细流行病学图谱。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明需要有针对性的诊断策略,例如用于中枢神经系统测试的脑脊液细胞增多门控、分层呼吸算法和不可亚型甲型流感的强制反射测序,以提高诊断的适当性和针对潜在人畜共患流感威胁的监测。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和单中心设置而受到限制,这可能会影响普遍性。然而,大样本量和全面的分析为当地诊断实践和 监测 协议提供了中等的证据强度。

Human rhinovirus/enterovirus dominated the respiratory ecology; influenza A was almost entirely H3 and H1N1pdm09, but 8.1% of influenza-A–positive specimens were equivocal or non-subtypeable and were never referred for sequencing, an avoidable surveillance blind spot for novel/zoonotic (avian) influenza. Pneumonia-panel resistance markers (mecA/C–MREJ, CTX-M, KPC, NDM) clustered in Enterobacterales co-infections. The gastrointestinal panel was dominated by diarrhoeagenic Escherichia coli pathotypes (chiefly EPEC and EAEC) and Clostridioides difficile toxin, its 77% negativity identifying a second over-utilised stream. We argue for CSF-pleocytosis gating, tiered/reflex respiratory algorithms, gastrointestinal-panel gating to community-onset diarrhoea, and mandatory reflex sequencing of unsubtypeable influenza A.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估意大利南部一家医院急性感染综合征多重 PCR 检测的 流行病学、诊断适当性和成本影响,重点关注阴性结果的高比例及其经济影响。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 对在 UOSD 微生物学和病毒学中心进行的所有 BioFire FilmArray 脑膜炎/脑炎 (ME)、上呼吸道 (RP2.1)、肺炎 (PN) 和胃肠道 (GI) 测定的回顾性分析。“Vito Fazzi”,ASL 莱切(意大利普利亚)于 2024 年 7 月 1 日至 2026 年 4 月 30 日期间进行,删除了重复测定以确保不同的诊断事件。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究涉及分析四个综合征组(中枢神经系统、上呼吸道、下呼吸道、胃肠道)的 5381 项测定结果,以评估病原体检出率、诊断适当性和耐药标记物,重点是识别可避免的 监测 盲点,例如无法分型的甲型流感。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在 5381 项测定中,每个目标的阴性率为 59.3%,阴性率因小组而异:ME 为 90.0%,GI 为 77.1%,上呼吸道为 44.2%,肺炎为 26.6%。中枢神经系统阳性主要是病毒(75%),以肠道病毒为首,肺炎链球菌是唯一一致的细菌病原体。甲型流感几乎全部是 H3 和 H1N1pdm09,但 8.1% 是模棱两可或不可分型的,并且未转介进行测序。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将高阴性率解释为过度使用某些组合的证据,特别是 ME 和 GI,并强调了不可亚型甲型流感的可避免的 监测 差距,这可能会错过新的或人畜共患的毒株。新颖之处在于跨多个综合征组的病原体分布和耐药模式的详细流行病学图谱。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明需要有针对性的诊断策略,例如用于中枢神经系统测试的脑脊液细胞增多门控、分层呼吸算法和不可亚型甲型流感的强制反射测序,以提高诊断的适当性和针对潜在人畜共患流感威胁的监测。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和单中心设置而受到限制,这可能会影响普遍性。然而,大样本量和全面的分析为当地诊断实践和 监测 协议提供了中等的证据强度。

title: Önem Kazanan Solunum Yolu Virüsleri ve Güncel Gelişmeler
abstract: Solunum yolu virüsleri son yıllarda artan tanı olanakları, yaşlı ve immün sistemi baskılanmış birey sayısının artması, değişen iklim koşulları, insan nüfusundaki artış, ulaşımın kolaylaşması ve bazı virüslerin pandemiye neden olabilme potansiyelleri nedeniyle giderek önem kazanmaktadır. Bu virüslerden özellikle respiratuar sinsityal virüs, influenza ve SARS-CoV-2 zatürreye neden olabilmekte, yaşlı ve bağışıklık sistemi zayıf hastalarda yaşamı tehdit edebilmektedir. Bunların dışında rinovirüs, adenovirüs, insan metapnömovirüsü giderek artan sıklıkta tanımlanan diğer solunum yolu virüslerindendir. Zoonotik kökenli virüslerin çeşitli mutasyonlarla insanda hastalık yapma özelliği kazanması ve salgınlara yol açmasını COVİD-19 ve Avian İnfluenza H5N1’de deneyimledik. Peki güncel tehditler ve gelişmeler neler? Bazı solunum yolu virüslerinden korunmak için aşı çalışmalarında ve tedavide umut verici gelişmeler mevcuttur. Yeni antiviral ilaçlar, monoklonal antikorlar ve aşı çalışmalarında durum ne? Bu genel derlemeyle önem kazanan solunum yolu virüslerinden bahsettik ve bu virüsler hakkındaki güncel gelişmeleri paylaştık.
journal: Kahramanmaraş Sütçü İmam Üniversitesi Tıp Fakültesi Dergisi

It highlights specific viruses such as respiratory syncytial virus, influenza, and SARS-CoV-2 that can cause life-threatening pneumonia in vulnerable populations, while also noting the increasing identification of other viruses like rhinovirus and adenovirus. The article references experiences with zoonotic viruses like COVID-19 and Avian Influenza H5N1, which have demonstrated the ability to mutate and cause human disease and pandemics. The review concludes by mentioning promising developments in vaccines and treatments for respiratory viruses, though specific details are not provided in this general overview.

title: Flu Mutation Explorer: an Interactive Platform for Mapping Host Adaptation Mutations in Influenza A Viruses
abstract: A rapid expansion of influenza A virus (IAV) genome sequencing has transformed global surveillance but has also created major challenges for interpreting the biological significance of viral mutations, particularly amino acid replacements associated with host adaptation. Resources have been created to support mutation annotation and phylogenetic analysis, but there is a need for a tool that integrates experimentally derived phenotypic evidence with evolutionary context in a framework suitable for users without prior training in bioinformatics. Here, we present the Flu Mutation Explorer, an interactive web application that combines large-scale influenza phylogenies with a manually curated database of reported mammalian adaptation mutations, to enable the exploration and interpretation of IAV genetic variation. The underlying database comprises over 1.5 million publicly available IAV sequences and over 1000 mutations associated with mammalian adaptation. The Flu Mutation Explorer enables users to query protein sequences, visualise amino acid distributions across viral lineages, examine host-specific conservation patterns, and identify adaptation mutation with links to supporting literature. We include case studies which demonstrate the platform's use in assessing amino acid conservation at sites of interest and in rapidly identifying candidate mammalian adaptation mutations during the ongoing H5N1 panzootic. By integrating genomic, phylogenetic, and functional information into an intuitive interface, the Flu Mutation Explorer lowers the barriers to interpreting influenza sequences for specialists and non-specialists alike.

title: Immunization with deglycosylated H7N9 VLP enhances cross-strain protective antibody responses against avian influenza H7N9 variants in mice
abstract: Introduction The rapidly evolving avian influenza H7N9 virus remains a threaten to public health globally. There is an urgent need to develop broad-spectrum vaccines capable of eliciting functional cross-strain protective immunity against emerging viral variants. Methods N-linked glycosylation can shield critical residues from immune recognition. Here, a prototype virus-like particle (VLP) was constructed based on the antigenic sequences derived from A/Taiwan/1/2013 H7N9 virus. Glycosidase enzymes were utilized to trim the glycan molecules for generating monoglycosylated VLP (VLPmg) and nonglycosylated VLP (VLPng) derivates. The structural integrity, antigenicity, and immunogenicity of these VLPs were systematically evaluated. Results Both VLPmg and VLPng maintained hemagglutination activity and antigenicity like the fully glycosylated prototype VLP (VLPfg). Immunization with deglycosylated VLPs induced robust virus-specific antibodies and a balanced Th1/Th2 immune profile in mice, whereas the titers were comparable to that of VLPfg. Among them, VLPng induced higher hemagglutination inhibition and neutralizing antibody titers against different H7N9 virus strains, indicating improved cross-strain reactive antibody responses. Conclusion This study demonstrated the enzymatic deglycosylation of influenza H7N9 VLP improves the induction of broadly protective antibody responses in mice. The nonglycosylated H7N9 VLP represents a potential vaccine candidate to against the threat of antigenically divergent H7N9 virus variants.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential of deglycosylated H7N9 virus-like particles (VLPs) to enhance cross-strain protective antibody responses against avian influenza H7N9 variants in mice. The research aimed to address the public health threat posed by the rapidly evolving H7N9 virus and the need for vaccines that can elicit broad-spectrum immunity. A prototype VLP was constructed from the A/Taiwan/1/2013 H7N9 virus, and glycosidase enzymes were used to generate monoglycosylated (VLPmg) and nonglycosylated (VLPng) derivates. Notably, VLPng induced higher hemagglutination inhibition and neutralizing antibody titers against different H7N9 strains, indicating improved cross-strain reactivity. The study concluded that enzymatic deglycosylation of H7N9 VLPs enhances the induction of broadly protective antibody responses in mice, suggesting that nonglycosylated VLPs may serve as a vaccine candidate against antigenically divergent H7N9 variants. However, the study is limited to in vivo experiments in mice, and the results may not directly apply to humans. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on animal models and the absence of clinical data.

title_zh: 去糖基化 H7N9 VLP 免疫可增强小鼠针对 禽流感 H7N9 变种的跨品系保护性抗体反应
source_body_en: Introduction The rapidly evolving avian influenza H7N9 virus remains a threaten to public health globally. There is an urgent need to develop broad-spectrum vaccines capable of eliciting functional cross-strain protective immunity against emerging viral variants. Methods N-linked glycosylation can shield critical residues from immune recognition. Here, a prototype virus-like particle (VLP) was constructed based on the antigenic sequences derived from A/Taiwan/1/2013 H7N9 virus. Glycosidase enzymes were utilized to trim the glycan molecules for generating monoglycosylated VLP (VLPmg) and nonglycosylated VLP (VLPng) derivates. The structural integrity, antigenicity, and immunogenicity of these VLPs were systematically evaluated. Results Both VLPmg and VLPng maintained hemagglutination activity and antigenicity like the fully glycosylated prototype VLP (VLPfg). Immunization with deglycosylated VLPs induced robust virus-specific antibodies and a balanced Th1/Th2 immune profile in mice, whereas the titers were comparable to that of VLPfg. Among them, VLPng induced higher hemagglutination inhibition and neutralizing antibody titers against different H7N9 virus strains, indicating improved cross-strain reactive antibody responses. Conclusion This study demonstrated the enzymatic deglycosylation of influenza H7N9 VLP improves the induction of broadly protective antibody responses in mice. The nonglycosylated H7N9 VLP represents a potential vaccine candidate to against the threat of antigenically divergent H7N9 virus variants.
abstract_zh: 简介 快速进化的 禽流感 H7N9 病毒仍然对全球公共卫生构成威胁。迫切需要开发广谱 疫苗,能够引发针对新出现的病毒变种的功能性跨毒株保护性免疫。方法 N-连接糖基化可以保护关键残基免受免疫识别。在这里,基于 A/Taiwan/1/2013 H7N9 病毒的抗原序列构建了原型病毒样颗粒 (VLP)。利用糖苷酶修剪聚糖分子,以生成单糖基化 VLP (VLPmg) 和非糖基化 VLP (VLPng) 衍生物。对这些 VLP 的结构完整性、抗原性和免疫原性进行了系统评估。结果 VLPmg 和 VLPng 均保持与完全糖基化原型 VLP (VLPfg) 一样的血凝活性和抗原性。用去糖基化的 VLP 进行免疫可以在小鼠体内诱导出强大的病毒特异性抗体和平衡的 Th1/Th2 免疫特征,而滴度与 VLPfg 相当。其中,VLPng针对不同的H7N9病毒株诱导了更高的血凝抑制和中和抗体滴度,表明跨病毒株反应性抗体反应得到改善。结论 这项研究表明,流感 H7N9 VLP 的酶促去糖基化可改善小鼠体内广泛保护性抗体反应的诱导。非糖基化的 H7N9 VLP 代表了潜在的 疫苗 候选药物,可对抗抗原不同的 H7N9 病毒变种的威胁。
